jobPostingInfo.title: Specialist, QA Monitoring, Vigilance & Market Surveillance - GL D - Defined Duration until December 2028
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
Specialist, QA Monitoring, Vigilance & Market Surveillance - GL D - Defined Duration until December 2028

The Global Fund aims to accelerate the end of AIDS, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria as epidemics. As part of our mandate to fight the three diseases, the Global Fund plays a leading role in global markets for medicines and technologies that prevent, diagnose, and treat HIV, Tuberculosis and Malaria. Every year, more than half of the Global Fund’s investments is used to procure key health products, ensuring they are available to those who need them most.

As one of the biggest health product procurement entities in the public sector, investing nearly US$3 billion in health products and equipment procurement, the Global Fund is uniquely placed to drive equitable access to quality-assured health products, services and innovations through its Supply Operations department.

Supply Operations, collaborating across the Global Fund Secretariat, is responsible for the Global Fund’s market shaping activities and the overall management of health product sourcing, procurement, quality assurance and supply chains.

The Quality Assurance & Compliance team plays a key function in ensuring safe access and delivery of quality assured health products to the communities and people we serve. This mission is implemented by enabling program and operational requirements, while mitigating residual risks associated with quality, safety and efficacy of health products procured with Global Fund funds through clearly established procedure, governance model and case management. The team works with external technical partners to keep the organization abreast of evolving matters related to health products QA requirements and compliance across public health sector.

The Specialist, QA Monitoring, Vigilance & Market Surveillance works under the supervision of the Manager, Product & Supplier QA Compliance. The Specialist supports the Global Fund’s mission by ensuring robust market surveillance and vigilance approaches are in place to monitor the quality, safety and efficacy of health products throughout their lifecycle. They ensure timely and appropriate management of health product related incidents downstream (post-shipment), with the assistance of the Associate Specialist, QA Case Management.

They analyze data and trends on all types of quality or safety or efficacy/poor performance information signals which can be of interest to assess potential risk for the quality of health products procured with The Global fund funds.

Based on information gathered and data analysis implemented, they propose, advise and support the implementation of the market surveillance strategy and programs in line with the emerging risk identified.

They contribute to country regulatory strengthening activities on vigilance and market surveillance.

Key Responsibilities

Policy and guidance

  • Contribute to the development and enhancement of The Global Fund’s (TGF) QA policies, guidelines and governance model.
  • Provide advice and support at all stages of grant design and implementation.
  • Contribute to the development of technical brief(s) or other supportive guidance documents to help applicants prepare their funding requests.

QA Monitoring, Market Surveillance & Vigilance

  • Contribute to the technical support provided to countries in order to ensure implementation of TGF Market surveillance and vigilance activities.
  • Support QA compliance monitoring activities by linking vigilance findings with broader product quality assurance efforts, including supplier and PSA compliance verification.
  • Working closely with the Associate Specialist, QA Case Management, lead the analysis of quality and safety signals, and contribute to risk mitigation strategies in collaboration with country teams and the QA & Compliance team.
  • Analyze data and potential trend on all types of quality or safety or efficacy/poor performance signals.
  • Contribute to the assessment of potential risk for the quality of health products procured with TGF funds in close collaboration with the relevant health product QA Specialist.
  • Propose, advise and support implementation of market surveillance strategy and programs in countries in line with the emerging risk(s) identified and ensuring market surveillance activities or safety events are reported to Global Fund QA.
  • Contribute to country capacity building by supporting the development of national vigilance systems, training programs, and regulatory frameworks for market surveillance.
  • Contribute to the selection of service providers on Regulatory, Quality Assurance and quality control matters including market surveillance and vigilance.
  • They lead the investigations of quality complaints, safety events and other quality challenges experienced by Global Fund Principal Recipients and advise QA Team Lead on optimal risk-mitigation measures
  • Coordinate the product recalls with internal stakeholders and national regulatory bodies in case of non-compliance of healthcare products procured with Global Fund funds.
  • They contribute to the assessments of country risk for downstream QA-related processes, and advise and support relevant in-country risk mitigation measures

Partnership

  • Support coordination and interaction across Supply Operations teams, for an aligned approach on Market surveillance and vigilance.
  • Collaborate with Technical Advice and Partnerships (TAP), Risk, and Grant Management divisions to ensure alignment of vigilance and market surveillance activities with grant implementation and risk mitigation strategies.
  • Contribute to regular feedback sessions with WHO and other Partners to improve sharing of information on Market surveillance and vigilance.
  • Support partnership and coordination on Market surveillance and vigilance.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of QA management system that is well integrated with the Global Fund’s enterprise resource management ecosystem to enable advanced analytics, performance monitoring and KPI reporting.
  • Contribute to strengthening collaboration and effective communication between the QA & Compliance team, other teams within Supply Operations and teams in other Global Fund divisions / departments such as Grant Management, Technical Advice and Partnerships (TAP) and Risk on shared priority initiatives and activities.

Subject to change by the Executive Director at any time at their sole discretion.

Qualifications

Essential:

  • Advanced university degree in Pharmacy, Chemical Engineering, and/or life science or an equivalent combination of academic/professional qualifications and experience within the area of Quality Assurance & Regulation.

Desirable:

  • Project management, process improvement or organizational change qualifications
  • Certification in medical vigilance and pharmacoepidemiology
  • Knowledge in ISO 13485, 2859-1 &-2, 17025.

Experience

Essential:

  • Leadership and People management
  • Minimum 5 years working experience in QA management in the private or public sector.
  • Experience within regulatory system within global public health.
  • Experience with external partner engagement in a multilateral context, with e.g., UN agencies, International NGOs and Donors on QA matters.
  • Work experience in developing and implementing Market surveillance strategies.
  • Work experience with a major multilateral organization.
  • Experience in matrix organizations and working in cross-functional teams.

Desirable:

  • Minimum 10 years of working experience in QA management or regulatory affairs.

Competencies

Languages:

An excellent knowledge of English and preferably a good working knowledge of French. Knowledge of other languages would be an asset.

Functional Competencies:

  • Legal-Lev1
  • Geopolitical Awareness-Lev2
  • Communications- Lev2
  • Negotiation -Lev2
  • Procurement and Supply Chain- Lev2
  • Risk -Lev2

The Global Fund recruits top-tier talent for our open positions, in support of our mission to end AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria as epidemics.

 

Explore our vacancies and apply on the Global Fund Careers recruitment system.

 

More information on working at the Global Fund is available on the Careers section of our main website.

Job Posting End Date

16 September 2026

jobPostingInfo.title: 2026 Research Analyst
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
Work for the IMF. Work for the World.

 

The Fund seeks dynamic and highly motivated Research Analysts (RAs) with strong quantitative and analytical skills.

The successful candidates should have the proven ability to work independently, as well as collaboratively in a team environment. The RAs will be responsible for a wide range of support including, but not limited to, data gathering, econometrics, analysis of economic or statistical data sets, and basic programming for high-quality analyses.

This is a contractual appointment for one year, renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, depending on the business need and performance of the incumbent.

Research Analyst positions are filled with candidates physically residing in the local Metropolitan Washington, D.C. area.


Job Summary

Supports departmental objectives on economic analysis and managing information technology & systems. Analyzes and computes statistical and economic data in support of the department. Additionally, the RA will manage Fund database(s) and contribute to staff reports.

This opportunity may meet PREDOC requirements for applications to subsequent academic study.


Major Duties and Responsibilities

Compiles statistical data, compares and evaluates alternative data sources, and ensures consistency of series and definitions.

Computes data collected using statistical and econometric techniques and develops summary analysis, including summary tables and charts for various reports.

Develops and maintains comprehensive and fully documented cross-country databases in accordance with Fund-wide data management requirements on an ad-hoc basis.

Maintains relevant computer software, and writes, updates, modifies, and executes computer programs for statistical and econometric analysis. Initiates analytical work, especially the econometric analysis, underpinning the work of relevant papers and publications produced by the work unit. Participates in divisional/departmental research projects and drafts targeted notes on selected issues of relevance to the division's /department’s work program. Participates in occasional departmental missions and liaises with country authorities, academia, or financial institutions.


Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science or other related quantitative field, but more competitive candidates would have a Master’s degree in the relevant field.

Two years of relevant work experience in a similar role.

  • Proficiency in MS Excel, including basic functions and formula.

  • Proficiency in the use of analytical, statistical and econometric software packages such as STATA, EViews, R, TSP, SPSS, Matlab and SAS.

Preferred:

  • Experience working with finance, budget, people analytics, macroeconomic data and writing macroeconomic research reports.

  • Experience and ability to use a range of visual presentation tools such as PowerPoint, MS Excel charts, Tableau, Keynote, Prezi and other similar tools.

  • Familiarity with database management tools such as: Power BI, SQL, MS Access, IBM Cognos BI.

  • Knowledge of Python, C++, and other similar programming tools would be a plus.

In addition, the following competencies are critical to the position:

  • Proven ability to manage large and complex databases and develop summary analysis, including summary tables and charts, and sound analytical and problem-solving skills, including a knowledge of statistical applications and techniques.

  • Sound organizational and data management skills, and ability to handle several responsibilities and work under tight time constraints.

  • Ability to work without direct supervision, paying close attention to details and bearing independent responsibility for data accuracy.

  • Proven experience in dealing with all levels of staff in responding to a wide range of inquiries.

  • Ability to use tact, discretion, and sound judgment when dealing with clients and in handling confidential information.

Department:

Hiring For:

A06, A07, A08

The IMF is guided by the principle that the employment, classification, promotion, and assignment of staff shall be made without discrimination against any person. We welcome requests for reasonable accommodations for disabilities during the selection process. Information on how to request accommodations will be provided during the application process.

jobPostingInfo.title: Senior Policy Advisor - Geoeconomics and Digital Assets
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
We don’t just talk, we do. Lead the change with us.

At the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, we work with political leaders around the world to drive change. We help governments turn bold ideas into reality so they can deliver for their people. We do it by advising on strategy, policy and delivery, unlocking the power of technology across all three. And by sharing what we learn on the ground, so everyone can benefit. We do it to build more open, inclusive and prosperous countries for people everywhere.

We are a global team of over 800 changemakers, operating in more than 40 countries, across five continents. We are political strategists, policy experts, delivery practitioners, technology specialists and more. We speak more than 45 languages. We are working on over 100 projects, tackling some of the world’s biggest challenges. We’re all here at TBI to make a difference.

In a world of ever more complex challenges, we believe diversity of background and perspective is a strength. We pride ourselves on a culture that values and nurtures difference. We are dedicated to unlocking potential, not only for the countries we work in but also for each of our team members. No matter where you’re from or who you are, if you’re passionate about the transformative power of progressive politics, we invite you to build a better future with us.

Role Summary

Key Responsibilities

Policy Leadership & Research

  • Lead TBI's research programme on geoeconomics and digital assets.
  • Develop original policy papers, reports and strategic analysis on digital assets, stablecoins, tokenisation and sovereign digital financial infrastructure.
  • Assess how emerging financial technologies are reshaping geopolitical competition, monetary sovereignty and international finance.
  • Translate complex economic and technological developments into practical policy recommendations for governments.

Government Advisory

  • Advise political leaders, ministers and senior government officials on digital finance policy and strategic implications.
  • Support governments in understanding policy choices relating to sovereign digital financial infrastructure.
  • Develop briefing materials and policy recommendations for senior decision-makers.

Thought Leadership

  • Position TBI as a leading global voice on geoeconomics and digital finance.
  • Publish research, opinion pieces and policy commentary.
  • Represent TBI at international conferences, roundtables and policy forums.
  • Build relationships with leading academics, think tanks and international organisations.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build relationships across governments, regulators, central banks, multilaterals and industry.
  • Convene expert working groups and policy discussions.
  • Collaborate across TBI's policy, technology and delivery teams.

Internal Leadership

  • Provide subject matter expertise across TBI.
  • Mentor junior colleagues contributing to the research agenda.
  • Support the development of future policy capability in digital finance and emerging technologies.

Team management and internal coordination

  • Perform other duties and assignments as reasonably requested, supporting the successful delivery of TBI’s strategic objectives and operational priorities.
  • Provide support and cover for colleagues during periods of leave, absence, or peak workload, ensuring the effective delivery of team and organisational objectives.

Person Specification

Experience & Track Record

  • Significant experience in geoeconomics, international political economy, digital assets, financial innovation or financial policy.
  • Experience producing high-quality policy research or strategic analysis.
  • Experience advising governments, international organisations or senior policymakers.
  • Strong understanding of geopolitical trends affecting international finance.

Technical Expertise

Strong understanding of:

  • Digital assets
  • Stablecoins
  • Tokenisation
  • CBDCs
  • Digital financial infrastructure
  • Financial market infrastructure
  • International financial systems
  • Geoeconomics
  • Economic statecraft
  • Emerging technologies and their policy implications

**Please note that you must have an existing right to work in the United Kingdom to apply for this role.

jobPostingInfo.title: Technical Advisor - National AI Strategy
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
We don’t just talk, we do. Lead the change with us.

At the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, we work with political leaders around the world to drive change. We help governments turn bold ideas into reality so they can deliver for their people. We do it by advising on strategy, policy and delivery, unlocking the power of technology across all three. And by sharing what we learn on the ground, so everyone can benefit. We do it to build more open, inclusive and prosperous countries for people everywhere.


We are a global not-for-profit organisation, operating in more than 40 countries across five continents. Our teams include political strategists, policy experts, delivery practitioners, technology specialists and more. We speak more than 45 languages and are working on over 100 projects, tackling some of the world’s biggest challenges. We’re all here at TBI to make a difference.


In a world of ever more complex challenges, we believe diversity of background and perspective is a strength. We pride ourselves on a culture that values and nurtures difference. We are dedicated to unlocking potential, not only for the countries we work in but also for each of our team members. No matter where you’re from or who you are, if you’re passionate about the transformative power of progressive politics, we invite you to build a better future with us.

Role Summary

Introduction

TBI is partnering with Ghana's Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations (MoCDTI) to support implementation of Ghana's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2035. The programme will establish an Embedded Technical Assistance Facility within MoCDTI, combining a full-time adviser in the Minister's Office with support from TBI's Ghana team, global AI and digital-government specialists, and Ghanaian and UK partners including the KNUST Responsible AI Lab, the London School of Economics, Imperial College London and the UK Government Digital Service. The aim is to help government move from strategy to coordinated, responsible and measurable implementation across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs).

Candidates will need to have the existing right to work in Ghana, as unfortunately we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Role Overview

The Embedded Technical Adviser & Project Coordinator will lead the day-to-day coordination of TBI's contribution to this engagement. Seconded full-time to MoCDTI, the adviser will work directly within the Minister's Office and relevant directorates as a trusted strategic and delivery partner. The role will support the Minister and Ministry leadership to set priorities, translate the National AI Strategy into implementation roadmaps and annual plans, coordinate delivery across government, strengthen governance and reporting mechanisms, and accelerate a focused portfolio of high-impact public-sector AI exemplars.

The adviser will work with TBI's Ghana team and the wider expert network; maintain the programme's workplan, milestones, dependencies, risks and reporting routines; and ensure that specialist inputs are converted into practical decisions, tools and institutional capability. Detailed priorities and deliverables will be agreed with the Minister during inception and reviewed with MoCDTI and TBI as implementation evolves. Core outputs will be co-developed with government counterparts, TBI's delivery team and the wider expert network rather than produced by the adviser in isolation.

This is not a conventional IT implementation or research role. It requires a technical adviser who can move fluently between political and policy advice, programme management, institutional reform and technically informed AI delivery. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating in an embedded government environment, briefing senior political principals, working through public-sector systems and ambiguity, and transferring knowledge to permanent government counterparts.

Key Responsibilities

  • Act as the day-to-day strategic and delivery adviser to the Minister and MoCDTI leadership on implementation of Ghana's National AI Strategy, including prioritisation, sequencing, decision support and resolution of delivery bottlenecks.

  • Lead mobilisation and day-to-day programme coordination: prepare the inception report and detailed workplan; agree deliverables and ways of working; maintain milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions and escalation routes; and coordinate regular engagement between the Minister, MoCDTI and TBI.

  • Coordinate development of the National AI Strategy implementation roadmap, annual delivery plans and national- and MDA-level performance framework, including clear owners, KPIs, dashboards and quarterly implementation reporting.

  • Coordinate whole-of-government implementation across MDAs and the AI focal-point network, aligning sector-specific activity with a common national direction and facilitating collaboration, accountability and problem solving.

  • Support MoCDTI to design and operationalise the AI Council/Responsible AI Office and related governance mechanisms, including mandates, operating procedures, responsible AI standards, data protection, security, risk management and issue escalation.

  • Support an across-government AI exemplar programme. Work with MoCDTI and participating MDAs to select priority initiatives based on strategic relevance, public value, feasibility, data and institutional readiness, responsible AI considerations and potential to scale; then support feasibility assessment, implementation planning, ownership and monitoring.

  • Develop practical implementation toolkits and guidance for MDAs, covering use-case prioritisation, readiness assessment, data governance, infrastructure and model choices, procurement, delivery stage gates, risk management and benefits measurement.

  • Produce and coordinate high-quality ministerial and senior-facing products, including policy briefs, cabinet submissions, decision notes, strategic communications, meeting materials and implementation reports, working through the agreed TBI-MoCDTI quality-assurance process.

  • Convene and coordinate with TBI's Ghana team, global AI and digital-government specialists and partner institutions - including LSE, KNUST-RAIL, Imperial College London, the UK Government Digital Service and other experts - ensuring specialist inputs are well scoped, timely and translated into practical government action.

  • Build sustainable capability within MoCDTI and participating MDAs through embedded coaching, mentoring, problem-focused workshops, policy dialogues, reusable tools and structured handover to permanent government counterparts.

  • Strengthen the wider AI ecosystem and partnership pipeline by engaging government, academia, industry, civil society and development partners; support investment cases, technical and financial resource mobilisation, cost-and-savings analysis, and Ghana's positioning as a regional leader in responsible AI implementation.

Person Specification

We are looking for an exceptional public-sector adviser and delivery professional with a strong record of turning policy and technology strategies into implementable government programmes. The successful candidate will combine political judgement, delivery discipline and sufficient technical fluency in AI and digital government to work credibly with ministers, civil servants, engineers, researchers and development partners.

The successful candidate will have:

Essential

  • Substantial senior-level professional experience in public-sector advisory, government delivery, digital transformation, institutional reform, management consulting, international development or a comparable environment.

  • A demonstrated track record of advising ministers, political principals and/or senior civil servants, and translating political and policy priorities into clear decisions, plans and accountable delivery actions.

  • Experience leading or coordinating complex, multi-stakeholder government programmes from strategy through implementation, using workplans, milestones, KPIs, dashboards, risk and issue management, and structured reporting.

  • Strong working knowledge of artificial intelligence and digital government, including public-sector use cases, data and infrastructure dependencies, responsible AI and governance, and implementation and procurement risks. The role does not require a software engineer, but it does require the ability to challenge, mobilise and integrate technical specialists.

  • Strong knowledge of Ghanaian or other African government contexts, with the political economy and institutional judgement required to navigate public-sector systems and build durable government ownership.

  • Excellent analytical, policy-development and writing skills, with evidence of producing clear senior-facing briefs, cabinet or decision papers, implementation roadmaps, presentations and progress reports.

  • Exceptional stakeholder-management, diplomacy and facilitation skills, with the ability to convene and align MDAs, development partners, academia, civil society, industry and technical experts.

  • The judgement, discretion and resilience to operate at pace in an embedded government environment, manage ambiguity and sensitive information, and build trust with senior counterparts.

  • Strong programme coordination, organisation and follow-through, including the ability to prioritise competing demands and coordinate inputs from dispersed internal and external teams.

  • A practical commitment to knowledge transfer, mentoring and institutional capability building rather than dependency on external advisers.

  • An advanced degree in public policy, public administration, economics, international development, technology, engineering, computer science, business or a related field, or equivalent practical experience; excellent written and spoken English; and willingness to be based full-time in Accra and travel as required.

Desirable

  • Direct experience working with the Government of Ghana, MoCDTI or Ghana's wider digital and AI ecosystem.

  • Experience implementing a national AI, digital-government, data, digital public infrastructure or public-service transformation programme.

  • Deeper expertise in one or more of responsible AI, data governance and protection, cybersecurity, digital procurement, regulatory design or institutional governance.

  • Experience with technical-assistance or grant-funded programmes, including results frameworks, value-for-money analysis and programme reporting.

  • Established relationships across Ghana's technology and AI ecosystem, academia, industry, civil society and development-partner community.

  • Experience supporting public-sector AI use cases, feasibility and readiness assessments, business or investment cases, cost-benefit analysis, or technical and financial resource mobilisation.

  • A recognised project, programme or change-management qualification, and experience using AI-enabled and digital collaboration tools responsibly to improve delivery quality and productivity.

Closing Date:

2026-09-21

Background :
Le Système des Nations Unies (SNU) en Tunisie a élaboré sa Stratégie des Opérations (BOS) pour renforcer la collaboration entre les agences onusiennes présentes dans le pays et assurer une gestion efficiente et transparente des ressources. Pour soutenir la mise en œuvre de cette stratégie, le SNU s’appuie sur son agence opérationnelle, le Bureau des Nations Unies pour les services d’appui aux projets (UNOPS), qui recrute le personnel chargé d’assurer la sécurité des locaux situés à Tunis et à Zarzis.
L’UNOPS, bras opérationnel des Nations Unies, fournit des services spécialisés en gestion de projet, passation de marchés et infrastructures, contribuant ainsi à l’efficacité et à la durabilité des projets de ses partenaires
Mission du personnel de sécurité. Le personnel de sécurité est responsable de la protection des personnes, des biens et des installations
techniques sur les sites des agences du Système des Nations Unies (sièges, ou centres). Sa mission s’inscrit dans une logique de prévention, de vigilance et d’intervention, contribuant directement à la sûreté des opérations et à la sérénité du personnel.

jobPostingInfo.title: Account Manager, Partner Strategy, India and South Asia
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
Please Note: This role requires the ability to work on site 3 days per week per company policy.

The World Economic Forum, committed to improving the state of the world, is the international organization for public-private cooperation.

The Forum engages the foremost political, business and other leaders of society to shape global, regional and industry agendas.

Why we are recruiting:

As a partnership organization and through the Business Engagement teams, the World Economic Forum engages the private sector to address industry, regional and systemic issues. Partners benefit from and contribute to the global knowledge base through working closely with the Forum to set the intellectual agenda of Forum gatherings, drive the insight agenda of its publications and steer the impact of its initiatives.

Structured geographically, the Regional Business Team is responsible for building and managing the world’s premier communities of business executives from emerging markets, and seek to bring diversity, inclusion, and relevance to global industry conversations.

We are currently seeking a Partner Lead (account manager), India & South Asia, who will be tasked with supporting partner engagement and retention. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio composed of some of India’s largest and most relevant companies across industries including energy, health & healthcare, financial services, information technology, mobility, collaborating with corporate executives to determine and deliver on year-round engagement plans. Overall, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to fundamentally shape the quality of engagement of the World Economic Forum’s partner portfolio in India.

Reporting Lines and Interactions

jobPostingInfo.title: Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
The World Economic Forum, committed to improving the state of the world, is the international organization for public-private cooperation.

The Forum engages the foremost political, business and other leaders of society to shape global, regional and industry agendas.

Why we are recruiting?

The Forum is building world-leading digital collaboration platforms, knowledge and data tools, and digital event experiences for our constituents. As part of the evolution of our engineering operating model, we are moving from technology-vertical teams to durable, cross-functional product teams supported by horizontal engineering practices. We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the people and the outcomes of one or more of these product teams: owning delivery, developing the people, building the culture, and clearing the path for the team to do its best work.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will remain close to the code — contributing directly to product development — while being co-responsible, together with the Product Lead, for the delivery, quality and business impact of your team’s work.

Reporting Lines & Interactions

Part of the Forum IT Team, the Engineering Manager reports to the Product Engineering Lead. You will partner closely with a Product Lead and Product Managers on roadmap and priorities, collaborate with Practice Leads who steward platform standards and hold the technical bar in hiring, and work alongside an embedded Quality Engineer within your product team. You will also coordinate with fellow Engineering Managers to ensure cross-product engineering alignment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Partner with the Product Lead on roadmap and priorities, taking co-responsibility for the outcomes of the product team — delivery, quality and business impact.
  • Lead hiring of engineering resources for the team, run high-quality 1:1s and performance reviews, and own headcount planning for your team.
  • Develop the people and the culture: coach engineers on skills and growth, resolve conflicts within and across teams, and foster a continuous learning environment.
  • Stay technically credible and close to your team’s day-to-day engineering work by supporting design decisions, reviewing code, and contributing hands-on where it adds value to delivery and quality.
  • Drive the technical analysis of new projects and features within your product team, ensuring solutions are well understood, feasible, and aligned with agreed engineering standards. Partner with Practice Leads to surface platform-specific needs, technical debt, architectural risks, or cases where divergence from paved paths may be required.
  • Ensure agent-assisted development workflows and paved paths are effectively adopted and used in day-to-day delivery, and maintain cross-product engineering alignment with peer Engineering Managers.

Requirements

  • University-level degree in computer science, engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 7+ years of relevant industry experience in software engineering, including 2+ years leading and managing engineering teams with a proven track record of shipping digital products.
  • Demonstrated people-leadership skills: hiring, coaching, performance management, and conflict resolution across cross-functional teams.
  • Strong command of at least one major API/web development language and framework — such as Node.js, Python, Ruby on Rails, or Go — with the breadth to read, review, and contribute across related product engineering domains.
  • Ability to shape end-to-end solution architectures across product experiences, APIs, data, integrations, quality, security, and operations.
  • Comfort with RESTful APIs, service-oriented architectures, relational, document, and vector databases. Familiarity with frontend, mobile, Salesforce, automated testing, CI/CD, and release readiness practices is a strong advantage.
  • Practical experience with agent-assisted (AI-assisted) development workflows and a strong point of view on how they change team productivity and quality.
  • Experience working in structured, Agile delivery environments with issue-tracking tools such as Jira, in close partnership with product management.
  • Exceptionally clear documentation and communication skills, with the ability to thrive in a complex, international organization.
  • Fluency in English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Why join us?


Join an independent and impartial organization with over 55 years of connecting leaders to make sense of global challenges and move the world forward together.

ORGANISATIONAL CONTEXT:

In 2018, WFP re-established its presence in the Caribbean with an office in Barbados.   • Finance - To support effective delivery of finance, budget and administration support services in order to facilitate transparent and efficient utilization of financial resources.

  • Logistics - To implement well-defined standard logistics/supply chain processes and activities to enable effective delivery of goods and services for all delivery modalities.

  • Procurement - To perform and apply appropriate processes, procedures and policies that support the efficient and effective procurement services.

  • Information Technology - To deliver high quality technical support, system and data maintenance across a range of areas, in order to contribute to the effective delivery of IT services.

  • Communication - To perform general administrative and some specialised communications processes that support the creation of communications content and the delivery of communications services aimed at maintaining and enhancing WFP’s visibility and reputation and supporting fundraising activities.

jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS

20 September 2026-23:59-GMT United Kingdom Time (London)

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.

WHY JOIN WFP? 

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.

  • WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.

  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.

  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.

  • We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT

This position is part of Global Headquarters (GHQ) and reports to the Functional Director, or designate.

WFP focuses on macro insurance and insurance-linked securities to enhance preparedness and finance early action and emergency response. Its flagship initiative, ARC Replica, expands climate risk insurance coverage for millions while strengthening government capacity to respond to major climate shocks and integrate with adaptive social protection systems.

The macro insurance portfolio has grown to new regions and risk pools (CCRIF, PCRIC, SEADRIF), new market players (e.g., pilots in Syria and Afghanistan), and more catastrophic products (ARC and a World Bank Cat Bond). WFP is developing a Disaster Risk Financing (DRF) architecture to streamline this portfolio across corporate systems and to support a new UN DRF platform for inter-agency risk transfer.

WFP is a leading UN agency in this field, with over USD 102 million in pre-arranged finance for 2025 and active roles in the Insurance Development Forum and the Global Shield Coordination Hub.

Reporting to the Lead DRF Advisor in PRGR, this position sits within the DRF team, which supports micro, meso, and macro insurance initiatives and integrates innovative climate risk management tools into Country Strategies and climate adaptation projects funded by mechanisms such as the Green Climate Fund and Adaptation Fund.

THE ROLE

Based in the WFP London office, the role facilitates strategic partnerships with macro insurance partners (brokers, risk pools, insurance and reinsurance companies) and DRF actors (e.g., Center for Disaster Protection, the World Bank, Insurance Development Forum). The role increases WFP’s visibility with the UK government, IFIs, and the wider insurance sector, and contributes to designing and implementing the WFP DRF Architecture, the UN DRF platform, and the DRF4ASP window, including gender-responsive operational plans and a strengthened risk-layering approach.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority):

  • Partnerships: Develop and maintain effective technical and resource partnerships with key insurance stakeholders based in London – such as the World Bank’s Crisis and DRF London hub, The Centre for Disaster Protection, the Insurance Development Forum, Start Network (consortium of NGOs), and other partners (Lloyd's syndicates, brokers…). Identify opportunities to develop new partnerships with development, humanitarian and private sector entities to support more effective and efficient approaches to climate risk finance programming.

  • Strategic engagement: Ensure WFP's engagement on strategic discussions in the DRF sector and advise on developments on this topic which can effectively advance resource mobilisation for WFP's risk financing portfolio and more broadly for emergency preparedness and response.

  • Representation: Represent WFP in UN and other multilateral bodies, including NGO and private sector fora and provide these stakeholders with information on WFP’s disaster risk financing portfolio

  • Resource mobilization: Identify funding opportunities and develop proposals, advocacy and communication materials to increase WFP’s profile and support resource mobilization for DRF programmes from bilateral and multilateral public and private donors.

  • Technical supervision: Support country offices in the design and update of the risk profile, index insurance product, risk transfer parameters, and engagement with the insurance industry. Supervise the technical work and ensure that WFP purchases the best possible products to protect its operations against climate events and other disasters, and that governments have the best possible support regarding the design and implementation of their DRF strategy.

  • Capacity strengthening: Advise and support the development and delivery of functional training in disaster risk financing and insurance (DRF) to enhance the capacity of WFP staff at Global HQ and CO levels to design and deliver effective risk financing programmes, and strengthen governments stakeholders' capacities

  • Research & Evidence generation: Lead on the research and implementation of strategies for risk layering and improved early action in the context of the macro insurance programme, as well as the wider generation of evidence for ex ante approaches to disaster response. Develop and implement the learning strategy for macro insurance. Support the risk transfer research agenda for WFP in close collaboration with the Centre for Disaster Protection and other relevant research partners.

  • Operations, Preparedness and Response implementation: Oversee the implementation and continued scaling of WFP's macro insurance programme in the existing countries and prepare to expand to new countries or hazards over the course of WFP's next Strategic Plan (2026-2029).

  • Field work: Conduct country visits to introduce COs to macro insurance and DRF, with a focus on strengthening WFP and governments' response capacities, timelines and risk financing.

  • DRF architecture: Contribute to the design and implementation of the DRF architecture and to increase the amount of prearranged finance, as per WFP's target.

  • UN DRF platform : contribute to the coordination on the development of the platform with the other UN agencies, and humanitarian organizations (IFRC, Start Network), prepare necessary documentation to structure the project, engage with relevant stakeholders (IDF, CDP) who can support this initiative. Once the platform is operational, WFP's role will be clarified.

  • Budget management & Reporting: Plan use of resources, ensure that technical and financial reporting to donors is consistent and timely.

  • Any other tasks as required

QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE


Education: Advanced University degree in one or more of the following disciplines: economics, environmental studies, agriculture and food security, development studies, emergency preparedness or related area or First University Degree with two additional years of related work experience.


Experience:

  •     At least 8 years of post-graduate, progressively responsible work experience in disaster risk financing, parametric insurance, or climate risk management.

  •     Proven experience working with sovereign / macro risk financing instruments, with regional risk pools, insurance industry players (insurers, reinsurers and brokers), specifically on product design, policy placement, preparedness, payout implementation.

  •     Existing strong networks with key institutions in climate and disaster risk financing and insurance (CDRFI). Participation in working groups in this field.

  •     Existing experience working with UN organizations will be an asset.

  •     Field experience in humanitarian work.

Language: Fluency (level C) in English language. Intermediate knowledge (level B) of a second official UN language: Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, Spanish, and/or Portuguese (a WFP working language).

MORE ABOUT YOU

  • Strong expertise in climate risk financing / disaster risk financing / public finance management and operational experience in humanitarian preparedness & response to climate shocks or natural hazards.

  • Ability to lead high level technical discussions and advise senior partners. Experience in managing partnership and managing complex programming, including large budgets (above 5 m USD p.a)

  • Strong coordination and communication skills across diverse stakeholders. Excellent analytical writing and technical reporting skills.

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

  • This is an International Professional position and is open to all nationalities.

  • Mobility is and continues to be a core contractual requirement in WFP. This position is however classified as “non-rotational” which means the incumbent shall not be subject to the regular reassignment process unless the position is reclassified as rotational.

  • The selected candidate will be employed on a fixed-term contract with a probationary period of one year.

  • This position is open to both internal and external candidates.

  • WFP offers an attractive compensation and benefits package in line with ICSC standards (http://icsc.un.org) including basic salary, post adjustment, relocation entitlement, visa, travel and shipment allowances, 30 days’ annual leave, home leave, an education grant for dependent children, a pension plan, and medical insurance.

  • The selected candidate will be required to relocate to London, United Kingdom to take up this assignment.

WFP LEADERSHIP FRAMEWORK

 

WFP Leadership Framework guides to the common standards of behavior that guide HOW we work together to accomplish our mission.

Click here to access WFP Leadership Framework

 

REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION

 

WFP is committed to supporting individuals with disabilities by providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact:  global.inclusion@wfp.org

NO FEE DISCLAIMER

 

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

 

REMINDERS BEFORE YOU SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION

  • All applications must be submitted exclusively through our online recruiting system. We do not consider CVs or applications sent by email, LinkedIn, or any other channel.

  • We strongly recommend that your Workday profile is accurate and complete, and that all sections are filled in, including your employment history, academic qualifications, language skills, and UN grade (if applicable). Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application.

  • If you experience technical issues while submitting your application, you may contact us at global.hrerecruitment@wfp.org. Please note that this email is only for technical issues with an application - unsolicited applications or documents sent to this inbox will not receive a reply.

  • At the application stage, the only required documents are your CV and Cover Letter. Additional documents (passport, certificates, recommendation letters, etc.) may be requested later in the process.

  • Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

All employment decisions are made on the basis of organizational needs, job requirements, merit, and individual qualifications. WFP is committed to providing an inclusive work environment free of sexual exploitation and abuse, all forms of discrimination, any kind of harassment, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. Therefore, all selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks.


No appointment under any kind of contract will be offered to members of the UN Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions (ACABQ), International Civil Service Commission (ICSC), FAO Finance Committee, WFP External Auditor, WFP Audit Committee, Joint Inspection Unit (JIU) and other similar bodies within the United Nations system with oversight responsibilities over WFP, both during their service and within three years of ceasing that service.

jobPostingInfo.title: Intern
jobPostingInfo.jobDescription:
Application Deadline:

31-12-2026



 

The WTO Secretariat maintains three internship programmes for post-graduate students and recent graduates with an advanced university degree wishing to gain practical experience and deeper knowledge of the multilateral trading system. Only a limited number of such internships is available. Internship selections are based on merit, eligibility criteria, academic qualifications, and expertise.

The programmes, listed below, are designed to increase diversity at the WTO, and more information about each may be found in the links provided alongside:

(1) The WTO Internship Programme is open to post-graduate students and recent graduates with an advanced university degree from all WTO members and countries or customs territories engaged in accession negotiations - WTO Internship Programme

(2) The China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme  – Up to ten internships offered under this programme annually, RESERVED FOR POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS OR RECENT GRADUATES WITH AN ADVANCED UNIVERSITY DEGREE FROM DEVELOPING COUNTRIES AND LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES - China's LDCs and Accessions Programme

(3) the WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies - RESERVED FOR POST-GRADUATE STUDENTS FROM DEVELOPING COUNTRIES AND LEAST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES WORKING ON THEIR PH.D THESIS - WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies

RULES AND PROCEDURES FOR INTERNS (the following may vary, depending on the programme, so it is best to check the above links for information on a particular programme)


Eligibility:

A candidate must:

  • be a national of a WTO member state or a country or customs territory engaged in accession negotiations

  • have completed his/her undergraduate studies in a relevant discipline;

either:

    • be currently enrolled in a master's degree with at least one year completed; or

    • have completed a master's degree programme and be enrolled in a higher-level postgraduate programme (including doctoral studies); or

    • have completed a postgraduate degree (master's degree or PHD) within the past two years at the time of selection; and

  • be at least 21 years at the time of the internship (and no older than 30 years old at the time of the internship for the China WTO Accessions Internship Programme and China General Internship Programme).


A roster of suitable candidates is maintained from which interns are selected. In addition to the internship programmes, the need may also arise to recruit interns at short notice for specific tasks. These recruits will also be drawn from the roster. Names will be maintained on the roster for one year and no more.


Contractual Terms and Conditions:


An agreement will be established between the intern and the Director of the Human Resources Division, specifying the conditions of service and details of any remuneration.


Paid interns receive a daily allowance of CHF 60 (including weekends and official holidays falling within the selected period – Except for interns recruited under the China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme who will receive a daily allowance of CHF 90). No other remuneration of any kind shall be paid.


Internships take place in Geneva, Switzerland. Travel expenses to and from Geneva cannot be paid by the WTO (Except for the China's LDCs, Accessions and General Internship Programme and for the WTO Support Programme for Doctoral Studies), and such travel is not covered by the Organization's insurance. Interns are responsible for their own insurance cover for illness and accidents for the duration of the internship.

Please be aware that the cost of living in Geneva is quite high, and the allowance provided is intended as a supplement. It is important to ensure you have sufficient financial resources to support yourself during your time in the area.


Internships are for a minimum of three months and up to a maximum of six months in total with no extension, are dependent on the needs of Divisions, and may commence at any time during the year.  Depending on Divisional needs, an internship may be split between two Divisions (3 months and no less in each Division and not exceeding six months in total). In this case, the two internship assignments may be carried out at different times and not consecutively, as long as the applicant meets all the requirements for internship as per the "Eligibility" criteria set out above. It is not permissible to return to the programme at a later date after completing a full six-month internship programme, nor is it permissible to move from one programme to another following a six-month stint. An internship does not, in any way, entail the right to a vacancy in another part of the Secretariat. Interns may, nevertheless, apply to external vacancies.


While working at the WTO, interns are not considered as officials or staff members, however, they shall be bound by the same duties and obligations as regular staff members. Interns are expected to work full-time and to carry out the duties assigned to them by their supervisor.


On commencing the internship, and as applicable, depending on their nationality and any Swiss residence permit they may hold, interns may be issued with a Swiss legitimation card type "H" which serves as a work and residence permit for the duration of their internship. This link explains the responsibilities of holders of such a card and careful note should be taken of the information provided therein.


At the end of the internship, the Supervisor responsible for an intern will write an evaluation report, and the intern will also be required to evaluate the internship. Both evaluations will be placed on file.


An internship may be terminated by the WTO Secretariat or by the intern with one week's notice.
